note: Migne misprints a scripture reference. Policy (Wilson, 2026-07-18): the TEXT keeps what Migne prints (sacred-marker rule) and refDisplay stays verbatim, but refKey resolves to the CORRECT reference — the index must not propagate bad numbers. The key derived from Migne's printed form is retained as refKeyPrinted so every correction is auditable and reversible.
standard: OSIS book codes; chapter/verse follow the CITED (Vulgate) numbering, per scripts/index-work.mjs. Corrections here fix printer's errors ONLY — they never silently convert Vulgate versification to modern versification, which is a systematic divergence, not an error.

corrections.quote: Exiet Virga de radice Jesse, et flos de radice ejus ascendet
Jugum enim meum suave est, et onus meum leve
melior est finis orationis quam principium
corrections.note: Migne prints XVII for VII. The same verse is cited correctly as 'Eccles. VII, 9' at 1126c in this same work — internal evidence for the correction.

corrections.quote: omnes velit salvos fieri et ad agnitionem veritatis venire
corrections.note: Not Romans at all — the quotation is 1 Tim. 2:4.

corrections.quote: Bonum est nubere, melius est non nubere
corrections.note: The bene/melius comparison is v. 38, not v. 37. The wording is a compressed recast rather than the Vulgate text, but the verse is unambiguous.
Col. 4:2, not Matthew. Appears to be half of a transposition with the note following it.

corrections.quote: Quaerite, et invenietis; pulsate, et aperietur vobis
corrections.note: Matt. 7:7. Book right, chapter and verse displaced — the other half of the 73a transposition.

corrections.quote: Parati semper estote ad rationem reddendam
Verbum Christi habitet in vobis abundanter in omni sapientia
corrections.note: Colossians has only four chapters, so chapter V cannot exist. The quotation is Col. 3:16.

corrections.quote: Nolite thesaurizare vobis thesauros in terra ... Thesaurizate autem vobis thesauros in coelo
corrections.note: Matt. 6:19-20. The printed XIX, 20 looks like the chapter and verse have been transposed.

corrections.quote: Quicunque plus me fecerit domum, aut uxorem, aut filios, non est me dignus
corrections.note: Chapter right, verse wrong: 27 for 37. NB the quotation itself is corrupt (fecerit for a verb of loving; house and wife for father and mother) — the ENGLISH renders the corrupt line as printed and must NOT be conformed to Matt. 10:37.
There is no Third Corinthians. The lemma is 2 Cor. 6:2; the chapter numeral is right and only the book ordinal is misprinted, so the key stays chapter-level as Migne cites it.

corrections.quote: Si dixerimus quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos seducimus

corrections.note: Migne prints Ezeeh. for Ezech. (broken c). The host sentence names Ezekiel outright and the four living creatures are Ezek. 1, so the reference is not in doubt.

corrections.quote: Nescitis, quia templum Dei estis, et Spiritus sanctus habitat in vobis?
corrections.note: Migne prints the book without its numeral, so the reference does not parse at all. The quoted Latin is 1 Cor. 3:16 verbatim; II Cor. has no such verse.

corrections.quote: ad currendam viam, a summo coelo egressio ejus
corrections.note: A space split the Roman numeral: XV II for XVIII. The quoted words are Ps. 18:6-7 (Vulg.) — 'exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam; a summo caelo egressio eius' — so the reference is certain from the quotation itself, and no numeral is being reinterpreted, only rejoined. Printed form kept verbatim in the text and in refDisplay; the indexer could not parse the split numeral at all, so this is the difference between the citation reaching the scripture index and vanishing from it.

corrections.quote: Ipse super maria fundavit eam, et super flumina praeparavit illam
corrections.note: This is an INLINE (running-text) citation, column keyed on the OPENING paren per the 2026-07-31 inline-citation SPEC (the anchor 1121C falls inside it: '(Psal. [1121C] II)'). Migne prints II for the correct chapter; the quoted Latin — 'He founded it upon the seas, and prepared it upon the floods' — is Ps. 23:2 in the CITED Vulgate numbering (Ps. 24:2 modern), which has nothing in common with Ps. 2. Worked example 4 in data/inline-citations/SPEC.md.
